concepts.def: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for all θ. Derived from the unit circle. Source of related identities.
tan θ = sin θ / cos θ. Undefined when cos θ = 0 (θ = π/2 + kπ).
sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ = 2 cos²θ − 1.
Sine rule: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C. Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. Used in non-right triangles.
a cos θ + b sin θ = R cos(θ − α), where R = √(a² + b²), tan α = b/a. Useful for solving equations.
Angle measure where 2π rad = 360°. Arc length = rθ; area of sector = ½r²θ when θ in radians.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Trigonometry — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Trigonometry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Trigonometry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) depends on x and varies between 0 and 2.
